findings.text: The auto-generated `__rich_repr__` is only installed when `hasattr(cls, '__rich_repr__')` is false, and `angular` is only set on that generated function. `@auto(angular=True)` on a class that defines its own `__rich_repr__`, or on a subclass of an already-decorated class, silently ignores `angular`. Such a class still reprs as `Foo(...)` instead of `<Foo ...>`.

The generated `__rich_repr__` wraps every exception in `ReprError`, for example an `AttributeError` when `__init__` has a parameter such as `def __init__(self, x)` that is not stored as `self.x`. `repr(obj)` then raises instead of returning a string, which breaks debuggers, logging and tracebacks that call `repr()`. The `from None` also discards the original traceback.

0.reason: `angular` is only set on the generated `auto_rich_repr` inside `if not hasattr(cls, '__rich_repr__')`, so `@auto(angular=True)` is silently ignored when the class defines its own `__rich_repr__` or inherits one from a decorated parent (later upstream versions set `angular` outside this check).

1.reason: Wrapping the failure in `ReprError` is a deliberate design choice, and an `__init__` parameter that isn't stored on `self` would raise `AttributeError` from `repr()` anyway, so the wrapper doesn't make `repr()` fail where it would otherwise have worked.
